demand_source.title: Renew an adult passport | USAGov
demand_source.supports: The federal guide tells people to renew early because processing times vary and some countries and airlines deny entry when a passport has under six months left, which is the case for a long-lead reminder.

edits.description: A monthly text lists what is coming due, with the official link. Each item appears from the month its own lead time starts (a house choice of about nine months for an adult passport, shorter for a driver's licence, inspection, registration, domains and Global Entry); an item whose lead time is shorter than a month appears in the text for the month it falls due. A child's passport lasts five years and cannot be renewed, so its row says 'apply again in person'. The same table holds each child's yearly check-up, home and car upkeep on a repeat interval (furnace filter, oil change), the end date of a policy or warranty a parent asked Happy to file, and any tax, benefit or gift dates a parent typed in. Nothing is renewed, booked or paid.
edits.how: Preferred build, in the pattern of the model-free watchers (F018): one monthly host command job per parent (`--command-argv`, no model call) runs a reviewed script that reads the dates table generated from family.json5, plus household-store rows (F031) once parents can add them, works out in code which rows to list and prints one templated text, or `NO_REPLY` when nothing is due. A row is listed when its lead time has started or when it falls due before the next monthly run, so a row with a lead shorter than a month (a one-week gift date, a domain that renews in three weeks) is not skipped between two runs. The 9 Oct build note instead used a monthly isolated automation on the parent's agent with an empty tool list and the table in the job message; that leaves the date sums to the model, so keep it only as a fallback. Rows a parent adds by chat (a filed policy's end date, a typed benefit or gift date, 'did the furnace filter' restarting an upkeep interval) are written to the household store by the parent's own agent.
caveats: The build note has the dates table generated from Tony's registry, which a parent cannot change by chat. The carried-over extras that let a parent add a row ('file this as the car insurance policy', a typed benefit deadline) need either an edit by Tony or the household store (F031) as the table's home; decide which before building.

The text goes out once a month, so a lead time shorter than a month is not honoured to the day: a gift date with a one-week lead is named in the text at the start of its month, not a week before. A nudge on a particular day is an ordinary reminder (F007).
Reading a policy PDF to pull out its end date sends that document to the cloud model; whether that is acceptable is still an open decision.
If the fallback is used (a model run with no tools and the table in its prompt), the model works out the lead times itself and can get a date wrong; the script does the sums in code.
Command jobs are created by the operator and run on the Gateway host as the happy user, outside the sandbox, so the script is reviewed like the rest of the config repo.

edits.description: Checks that tell Tony, and only Tony, whether Happy is still sound: host-side, read-only scripts text him when something is broken or has changed (an expired or expiring sign-in, a failed channel probe, a plugin that did not load, a new audit finding, the firewall or FileVault off, a new listening port, automatic macOS update checks switched off) and carry his standing checklist (each month: spend caps, new stores in the backup, standing approvals; each quarter: the restore drill and key rotation). A few fixed cases in the existing eval suite also check Happy's behaviour after each change: no secret echo, no fake 'done', honest partial-failure reports, pending kept apart from done.

reason: Kept on OpenAI's guidance, reopened this round, that whoever deploys an agent should give its user a ledger of what it did and make after-the-fact actions easy to reverse. The build note never said where the 'saved 3 notes to memory' line comes from: memory saves use the built-in write and edit tools, not one of the in-house tools that keep the journal, so the note now names the hook that logs them, and the description says undo covers lists, reminders, the calendar and household facts, not a saved note.
who_trigger_result: Each parent, and Tony for forgetting / the Sunday job, a 'what did you do for me?' question, or 'undo that' / one text of what Happy did and saved that week, the last write reversed after a yes, and on request Tony clears what one conversation left in memory.

demand_source.title: Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems (OpenAI), section 4.4 Legibility of Agent Activity
demand_source.supports: OpenAI's guidance says it may be particularly important that whoever deploys an agent gives the user a ledger of what the agent did, as a lighter way than approvals to show a wider range of actions, and that actions reviewed only afterwards should be easier to reverse.

edits.description: Happy records every write it makes for a parent in one journal, so each parent can ask, or read in one Sunday text, what Happy did for them and what it saved to memory that week, and can say 'undo that' to reverse Happy's own last write to a list, a reminder, the calendar or the household facts from the past 24 hours, after seeing what will be reversed. Anything already sent (a text, an email, a print job) cannot be recalled, a saved note is corrected by asking Happy to change it, and clearing what one conversation left in memory stays Tony's job at the Mac, previewed first.
edits.how:
Journal (shared): each in-house write tool (household store, Reminders bridge, calendar write, the reminder-pinning hook) writes a row from inside the tool, where the old value is known: who asked, when, which tool, the inverse call. `openclaw audit --kind tool_action` gives names and outcomes only. Memory saves (F041) are made with the built-in `write` and `edit` tools, not an in-house tool, so their rows come from an observe-only `after_tool_call` hook on those two tools, filtered to the memory files: who, when, which file and the text saved, with no inverse. Approval rows come from the asking hook's `onResolution` callback. Review (G006, F085): a command automation renders the Sunday text with no model; a read tool returns only the asker's rows. Undo (CRT-01): an `undo_last` tool on `

-main`, limited by a `before_tool_call` hook to the requester's rows from the last 24 hours, shows the row, waits for a yes, runs the inverse; for a row with no inverse (a memory save) it says so, and the parent asks Happy to correct or delete the note. Forgetting (F085): `openclaw memory forget --agent --session --dry-run`, then without it, then hand-delete the `curatedWrites` lines.

who_trigger_result: Tony as operator / once, now, before any Mac or phone is paired, and again as the off switch during a pilot / a Gateway deny list that withholds screen control, shell, screen viewing and phone-data commands from every paired device, whatever tools an agent is later given.

demand_source.title: Computer use
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw's computer-use guide tells an operator who does not want screen control to put the command on the Gateway deny list, and says a denied command is withheld from the device and logged.

edits.how: Add `computer.act` to `gateway.nodes.commands.deny` in happy-config, and while no Mac node is wanted also every desktop host command the docs list as arriving with a Mac pairing: `system.run`, `system.run.prepare`, `system.which`, `browser.proxy`, `browser.proxy.upload.v1`, `mcp.tools.call.v1`, `screen.snapshot` and `desktop.stream`. A deny entry always wins over platform defaults and allow entries, matches exact command names, withholds the command (for `computer.act`, together with the node's `computer` capability) and is logged. The list is Gateway-wide, so the same change carries the phone ceiling for the iPhone app entry (OCL-01): deny the iOS default data commands (`location.get`, `contacts.search`, `calendar.events`, `reminders.list`, `photos.latest`, `motion.activity`, `motion.pedometer`) and the four push-to-talk commands (`talk.ptt.start`, `talk.ptt.stop`, `talk.ptt.cancel`, `talk.ptt.once`), which any node that advertises talk otherwise gets by default and which come off the list only when Talk (VOX-01) is set up; keep the opt-in commands (`camera.snap`, `camera.clip`, `screen.record`, `health.summary`, `contacts.add`, `calendar.add`, `reminders.add`) out of `gateway.nodes.commands.allow`, and set `gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled: false` so a paired device cannot publish tools to agents. Keep `computer` absent from every agent's tool lists; the per-person agents already deny `group:nodes`, which contains it, and the inbox agent denies every tool. Pairing is already manual-only in the config repo since M0 (`gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveLocal: false` and `sshVerify: false`; SSH-verified pairing is otherwise on by default), so keep both and do not use setup links for a Mac, since a setup link can still approve a node's first command surface automatically. The happy-inspect posture check reads only the first of the two; add `sshVerify`, the deny list and `pluginTools.enabled` to it. Leave `gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveCidrs` unset (it is off unless set), so no device is approved by network address alone. The deny list covers paired nodes; control of the Gateway's own desktop is a separate route that the docs say needs the `cua-computer` plugin explicitly enabled on the Gateway host, so never run `openclaw plugins enable cua-computer` on the Mac mini, and add a posture-check line that fails if that plugin shows as explicitly enabled, so the rule is checked and not only remembered. For reference, the documented gate stack for screen control is: tool policy exposes `computer` to an agent; gateway command policy; device pairing and then a second, distinct approval of the node's command surface; the switch inside the Mac app; and the macOS permissions. Exec approvals gate shell commands on a node, not clicks. Off switches during a pilot: (1) put the deny line back (command-policy changes reach connected nodes under the default hybrid reload, with no restart); (2) the G005 kill file checked in the desk hook; (3) on the Mac, turn off 'Allow Computer Control' (rechecked at each invocation) or revoke Accessibility.

who_trigger_result: Tony as operator today, a parent through their own agent later / Tony hands the desk agent one bounded test task (no family task is approved yet) / a short text result, with the screen work confined to a resettable virtual Mac that holds no accounts.
